In command appointments as a platoon commander, company commander and now battalion commander, I've commanded soldiers in Northern Ireland, the former Rhodesia, Bosnia and in other parts of the world. As a staff officer, I was a staff officer in an armoured brigade in NATO, I was a staff officer in Northern Ireland and I was a staff officer at our infantry school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you served in Bosnia. Could you give us a time frame for that service?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: I was recalled to my battalion to take up the post of second in command in late January '93. I arrived in Bosnia in early February, and I took up the appointment of second in command from about the 6th of February to about the 16th of May in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You say second in command, who was in command at that time?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: The commanding officer was Lieutenant Colonel Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you give us an idea, if you would, what the duties of a second command is?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: You're the deputy commander of the unit at that point, the one Cheshire group named as BritBat, part of the United Nations UNPROFOR force. My role was to shadow and mirror the commanding officer, to replace him in the event that he became a casualty. And my routine duties were to control the operational and information branches within the headquarters and to act as the de facto Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you describe, if you would, your general area of operation in Bosnia during that time period in early 1993?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, we had an area of responsibility. In the north was Tuzla. In fact, I'll explain what the size of our force was, then I can superimpose that on our area of responsibility. We were a battalion group of three infantry companies; a heavy weapons company, a reconnaissance company provided from a cavalry regiment; and a reconnaissance platoon of our own; and a battalion headquarters and echelon, the echelon being the logistics support. One company was based in Tuzla when I arrived in February. A company and the reconnaissance squadron were based in Vitez, and a company was based in Gornji Vakuf. And that essentially encompassed our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I'm going to ask for the assistance from the usher at this point, if I might. We have two maps over there on the wall if we could have them set up on the easel to help illustrate the additional testimony coming next. Can we have the first map marked as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are we going to get a copy of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have copies prepared.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first map will be Prosecution Exhibit number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If you will look at the exhibit marked number 5, and if would you, step up to that exhibit, there's a microphone there. If you would, would you describe what that map shows?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: The map shows the former Yugoslavia. And the highlighted square --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, if you would.

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: That's essentially the centre of our area of operations based on Vitez where our battalion headquarters and two manoeuvre units were, and the towns of Zenica, Travnik, Turbe, Busovaca, which were areas that we operated in and concentrated on from the 16th of April until we left on the -- in the middle of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, that yellow square, does that define your entire area of operation during that time period, or is it within your area of operations which is larger than that?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: It is within our area of responsibility. Our area of responsibility was considerably larger than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Would it be possible with perhaps your finger to give a general indication of your entire area of operation outside of that square?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: It's a little difficult without marking on the position of the Serbs at the time. But in very general terms, it went up through Zenica, Zepce, Maglaj at parts of Doboj and up to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Where was your headquarters during that time period?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: In the school just outside the town of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If you would remove that exhibit and look at the one behind it, and if we could have that exhibit marked, as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecutor's Exhibit number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That is now marked Exhibit number 6. Could you make a correlation between the square on exhibit number 5 and the map now designated Exhibit number 6?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: You have the Lazva Valley, the town of Vitez in the centre, and the main Vitez road that looped around to Zenica and the mountain road to Zenica and the road going north-west out to Vitez past our headquarters, which is here at Bila, and on up to Travnik. The map is familiar to me, this is exactly the scale of map we used when we were deployed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You mentioned the Lazva Valley; would you describe what you mean by the Lazva Valley?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: The valley through which the river Lazva flows, in our terms, Vitez was the centre of it. And the main sort of road that runs diagonally across the map up to Travnik and down around to the Zenica road. It was an area that became extremely well-known after the 16th of April. I knew it quite well up till then, although, other than liaising with the military commander in Vitez and the regional commander, whose headquarters was also in Vitez, Colonel Blaskic, I had no particular reason to know the hills around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned a road going through the Lasva Valley from Vitez to Zenica. Actually, I think you mentioned two roads.

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah. One we called the road to the dual carriageway and the other one we called the mountain road which went directly from Dubravica, at the junction just outside Vitez, up over the hills into Zenica, and running around the valley floor, along the Lasva Valley, until it joined at the dual carriageway junction, just where I'm pointing now (indicating), and the faster road there up to Zenica. Which road we took depended on the military situation and the weather.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You mentioned that road that goes along the Lasva Valley; not the mountain road, the other road. Did that road also go through the town of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: I always understood that Ahmici was north of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So it skirted along the edge of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah, and then went sort of further up into the hills on minor roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you often drive that route from Vitez along the Lasva Valley road past Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Innumerable times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Approximately how many kilometres is it from the centre of Vitez to the area of -- the Ahmici area, along that road?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Approximately four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Four kilometres? Yes. Now, you also mentioned Blaskic having a headquarters in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Who is Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Colonel Blaskic was the HVO regional commander for Central Bosnia reporting to Commander Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Just to get our terms straight. What is the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: The HVO was the military army of the Croat people of Central Bosnia, of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us where, if you recall, the HVO and Colonel Blaskic had its headquarters in Vitez, what building?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: In the Hotel Vitez, in the middle of the town along the main road on the right as we were transiting through from our school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, if you could, I would like you to look at the map on the easel behind the easel in front. It's a bit awkward, but perhaps the usher could assist in allowing you to do that.

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: The photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, the one behind. The one behind the easel. The big one, yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you ask the witness to speak into the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: We will actually need the easel in a minute. It's a little awkward, I'm sorry, but ... We would like to have this exhibit marked as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit, Prosecution Exhibit number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Watters, this may be a little confusing because I think things are flipped around a little bit on this map --

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: I can understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: -- so take your time, but if you could give us an idea of what that shows?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: It's an air photograph taken at an oblique angle of the area we have just been talking about with Vitez in the centre and then moving what is actually, I think, south, but going up the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: The sort of -- the road up to Kaonik, Busovaca, looping round to the Zenica road, and then the road either through Vitez or the Vitez bypass leading down to where our school was at Bila, and the village of Kruscica up here, which I know well, the village of Santici and Ahmici, which I know well, and the general topography of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Would you again show the Court, if you would, the road from Vitez along the outskirts of Ahmici that followed the valley, not the mountain road?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Right. From the centre of Vitez, which is here, you went up here through what was actually a sort of Croat-living area, over the bridge, onto the main road, which ran through the valley, you turn right and the road followed the valley until you reached this junction here, which was the road that led in towards Ahmici, and the road continued along the bottom end of Ahmici village until it made its way past the Busovaca turning, off to the dual carriageway leading to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Again, from the centre of Vitez to Ahmici is about four kilometres?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: That's about four kilometres, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned earlier about the Hotel Vitez where the headquarters for the HVO was located. Was that located in the centre of Vitez or in the outskirts of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: No, it's in the centre of Vitez. It's a little difficult, five years ago, on this scale, but I think that is probably as near as --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That was a multi-storey building, a fairly large building for that town?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: The entrance was actually along the road here, sort of pointing in this way, and the main bulk of the hotel went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, did Vitez have certain well-defined ethnic areas at the time you were in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, it did. I mean, they weren't necessarily manifest to us initially on our tour as it wasn't an area we focused on, but you had a sort of -- coming from this direction, from the north, you had a sort of mixed all-Croat area leading to a Muslim area here centred on a mosque, then up past the municipal buildings, the town hall I think was just about here where the mayor resided, and then this area here was Croat, north of the sort of Hotel Vitez, which was almost on sort of the interface between the Muslim sector of the town and the Croat sector of the town, and then with Croat houses here and then quite sort of well-to-do houses along this road here leading out of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: We are going to hand you a marker now, the usher will hand you a marker. If you could outline for us on that map the separate areas you've just described indicating the different ethnic areas in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: If I drew lines there (indicating) and about there, it's a bit rough, but that would show that area being Croat, this area being either mixed or largely Croat, and this area here being largely Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So the area, like a sandwich, in between those two other areas would be largely Muslim --

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: -- in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, what if you followed the road out of Vitez going towards Ahmici around that curve, right by that label saying "Vitez"? Would that area be Croat or Muslim?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: That would be Croat. The Croat area extended this way -- I mean, again, I wouldn't be able to point and say what house was what, but by and large, it was a wealthier area of the town and largely Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Following that road on to the T-junction, if you would, what was that area called, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: I can't remember, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you recall the Dubravica school, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah, that is about here, actually. That will be the Dubravica junction here, and the school was just north of the road leading up through Dubravica. It could actually be this -- it's this area here. It could actually be there (indicating). Again, on this scale, it's a bit difficult. Yes, again, that's the mountain road that leads to Zenica. So it would be this junction here, and the school was just north of the junction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I see. And that was simply an elementary school, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: I really couldn't answer that. It was just the school. There weren't very many children at school during this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Then continuing on up that road, you come into the area known as Santici and Ahmici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Were you familiar with a place known as the Bungalow?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That map is perhaps a little small, but take a look and see if you might be able to find it.

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: It's roughly in this area here (indicating). It could be there, it could be there. It's certainly that sort of area, to the best of my knowledge and memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Finally, having to impose on the usher one more time, we would like to do the blow-up of Ahmici and have the Colonel look at that for us a little bit. We would also like to mark this blow-up that will be put on the easel as our next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This exhibit has been marked as Prosecution Exhibit number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Watters, could you identify that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah. It's a blow-up of the previous air photograph concentrating on the junction off the main Lasva Valley road where it turned left into Ahmici. The cemetery was an obvious feature, Santici, and we had -- a United Nations Dutch battalion transport base was located somewhere around here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I see. Thank you, Colonel Watters. You may take a seat. At this time, we would like to offer into evidence those four exhibits. *** PLEASE SLOW DOWN FOR THE INTERPRETERS ***

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You are being asked by the interpreters to slow down. I just saw it on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry. At this time, I would like to show Colonel Watters three photographic exhibits and have them identified.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 7, 8, and 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If you might place that on the ELMO? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Watters, could you tell us what this exhibit shows?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: An overhead photograph of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Sort of a detail of downtown Vitez similar to what you showed us on the Lasva River Valley one?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: It may be difficult this many years later, but is it possible for you to pick out the headquarters of the HVO, the hotel?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah. I think it's this building here, it was the HVO regional headquarters. The town headquarters was in a cinema, and that was further back here somewhere, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I think we have a pointer that you can use. That's good.

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: This area here (indicating), to the best of my memory, is the Hotel Vitez, with the entrance off the main road here, and that was the regional headquarters of HVO and Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I see there's a road, sort of a long road that goes from left to right on the map. Would that be the main road that ultimately goes up to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Four kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I would like to show then the next photograph, as soon as the delivery has been made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you identify that for us, Colonel Watters?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: It's the side of the Hotel Vitez. The front of it is somewhere around here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And that would be where the headquarters of the HVO was located?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, it was, sir. I visited them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: This is essentially a close-up now of the actual building that was portrayed in that overhead aerial map we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: (No audible answer)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And then, finally, the third picture? Again, what does that show?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: That's the Hotel Vitez from the main road in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And that road, directly in front of it, is again, that main road that leads up to Ahmici and so forth?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Along the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us, Colonel Watters, when you first arrived in early 1993 in Central Bosnia, what was your mission and what was the mission of the British battalion at that time?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Our mission was to facilitate the distribution of humanitarian aid in our area of responsibility in order to prevent starvation and the degradation of the population of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And that's as best as I can remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: During the course of your stay in Central Bosnia, did the thrust of that mission change somewhat?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, it did. The essence of the mission remained unchanged and we distilled it to be the preservation of life. The thrust of the mission, from delivering humanitarian aid, as the military situation in Central Bosnia degenerated, that became more and more difficult and increasingly less relevant as the means of saving life was best achieved by interdicting and, where we could, preventing the fighting between the opposing forces, and by establishing cease-fires, monitoring cease-fires, and later establishing a cease-fire-monitoring mission based on the ECMM. We felt that we were achieving the implicit essence of our mission to save life because we no longer really could effectively distribute aid and, as I said, the distribution of aid was less and less relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Is there a particular day that comes to mind that sticks in your memory as to perhaps when your mission changed somewhat from merely delivering aid and assisting in the delivery of aid to actually saving lives in a more direct way?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: There were a series of situations that began to change the focus of our mission. Facilitating the movement of refugees from further Serb -- the fallout from further Serb attacks and the consolidation of Serb positions around Banja Luka caused us to spend a lot of time helping refugees through Turbe. Then the Serb positions in the pockets in eastern Bosnia, Srbrenica, our focus was heavily in Srbrenica in early April, and then within the centre of the area of responsibility, in the Lasva Valley, that changed abruptly on the morning of the 16th of April, '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Do you recall where you were early that morning, on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: I was in the headquarters in Bila school. The commanding officer was in Zenica investigating the kidnapping of a man called Totic who was the HVO police commander in Zenica, and he was overnighting in Zenica, sorting out how we could assist in finding Mr. Totic, as I was actually commanding the battalion at that time as he was at a radio communication, and I was in from about 3.00 in the morning, I was in the operation centre, as some strange things were happening. We were trying to understand what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You mention strange things were happening early in the morning on the 16th as you were the operations officer at your headquarters in Vitez. What sort of strange things did you begin to hear that early?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: The first thing that happened was a group of reporters came into the school asking for safety, basically. They had been staying in a sort of bed-and-breakfast accommodation. I think it's on the Vitez ring road, there was a garage, best known to us because there was a bear in a cage outside it, which we later sort of liberated, and these people reported that the door had been kicked into their room and masked men had ordered them to leave or they'd be killed, and they left all their belongings, got in their car and driven down to the school, and they were in a total state of shock. There had been an increase in criminal activity in the Lasva Valley, but that was quite unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You mention the ring road. This is a road that goes essentially or bypasses Vitez and goes around Vitez?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I take it these reporters were pretty scared when you saw them.

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: They were petrified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: What else happened early that morning?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: We began to receive reports of fighting and could hear very -- by about 6.00 in the morning, we could hear distant sounds of something like mortars or artillery in the direction of Vitez, and our echelon, which was closer to Vitez than we were, was reporting a considerable amount of heavy fire in and around the Vitez area and small arms fire all the way up the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: How were you getting these reports?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: From the static positions of our base leading in towards Vitez, at the junction of the main road into Vitez and the ring road, we had our echelon base and our petroleum point, and they were reporting it. And at about 6.00, I sent out some reconnaissance patrols up the Lasva Valley to report what exactly was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And when you say you sent out reconnaissance patrols, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: I mean pairs of Scimitar light tanks, or we call them CVRT, and pairs of Warriors to move up the road and report back what they see, not to actually interdict what they see, because they didn't have the combat power to deal with it, but just to report so we could get a picture of what was going on because it was very confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You mentioned Simtars as light tanks. Perhaps you might explain a little bit about what they are because we will be hearing about them again in the future?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: We have a generic vehicle within the British army called CVRT, and it has a number of specific-to-task vehicles, one of them is a reconnaissance vehicle, which is a two-man turret with a driver, a three-man crew all together, and it mounts a 30-millimetre rod-and-canon machine gun and it is our primary reconnaissance vehicle in the British army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: It is basically an armoured, tracked vehicle with a gun on it?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: It's a lightly armoured track vehicle. It can deal with small arms but can't take anti-tank fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You have, I think, another kind of vehicle at your disposal, a heavier kind of vehicle. Would you describe that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah. We were an armoured infantry battalion and it's based on 53 Warrior fighting vehicles. The Warrior is a substantially larger vehicle, it is a personnel carrier that carries eight fighting soldiers in the rear, a turret crew of two and a driver, and it has a higher degree of protection but is a much heavier vehicle and therefore not as --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness to slow down, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. It is not as manoeuvrable as the CVRT, as the Scimitar. We had 53 of those, and it was on those that our capability was based.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: But on the morning of the 16th, for purposes of reconnaissance, you sent out Simtars rather than Warriors?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: To be honest, sir, I can't remember. I think I sent out both. We had the reconnaissance squadron and "A" Company in Vitez at the time, and I would probably utilise both types of vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: When you say you sent them out throughout the Lasva Valley, could you be a little more specific on that, if you might? Where in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: I'd probably have to refer to our radio logs to be specific. Essentially, I just told them to go towards the sound of artillery and mortar fire and see if they could establish what on earth was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Did you get reports back after a while from these reconnaissance patrols?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah, for a couple of hours, I got reports of heavy fighting within Vitez and the hills above it, houses burning down the length of the Lasva Valley around Santici, Ahmici, and all the way up. The checkpoint that was normally at Dubravica was deserted as was the checkpoint at the bottom of the road where it joins the Zenica flyover, and they could hear a lot of small arms fire, and there was a report of an infantry assault in Vitez, a Croat infantry assault onto the sports centre, and it was still quite difficult from the radio reports to form a prognosis of what was happening because it was out of our area of familiarity. There had not been large-scale fighting in this area during our period, and I can't remember the exact time, but about 8.00, I took a patrol out myself just to try and get a feel for what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: This may be a good time to stop, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before adjourning, may I just draw the attention of Defence counsel to one of our guidelines? It's C, number 3, where we have stated: "Where possible, the Defence may consider appointing one of them to cross-examine a particular witness." I wonder whether they may consider this particular point tomorrow when cross-examining our witness. Before adjourning, let me also again ask the registrar to make sure that tomorrow at 9.30 sharp all the accused are here in court and also the witness should be here so that we can start right away. We will adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.30 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 5.30 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 18th day of August, 1998, at 9.30 a.m.
